pr_title: [Android][Fix] System Info displays empty/incorrect CPU info values
pr_body:
## Description
Implements some basic CPU info methods for Android.

Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/20619

## Motivation and context
System Info - Hardware displays empty/incorrect CPU info values. It seems that the functionality for Android was never implemented or worked differently before.

## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested on Nvidia Shield Pro 2019 (ARM64) and Android TV (ARM)

## What is the effect on users?
Provides some basic CPU info: model name, mips, frequency. ~Corrects wrong temperature indication (-1 ºC).~ 

Also improves logs info:

**Before**
```
2021-12-08 10:13:28.812 T:12633    INFO <general>: FFmpeg version/source: 4.4-Kodi
2021-12-08 10:13:28.812 T:12633    INFO <general>: 4 CPU cores available
```

**After**
```
2021-12-08 10:16:45.296 T:13108    INFO <general>: FFmpeg version/source: 4.4-Kodi
2021-12-08 10:16:45.296 T:13108    INFO <general>: Host CPU: ARMv8 Processor rev 1 (v8l), 4 cores available
```

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

**Before**
![screenshot00000](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/145184419-9c7dc517-e8d0-43f7-b3d9-1c7b6998af7d.png)

**After**
![screenshot00001](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/145184461-f75457b6-7e84-476f-b48b-8ae67008e184.png)

pr_comments:
Updated to use `CPosixFile` and checked that `GetCPUFrequency()` only is called one time when open hardware info (not auto-refreshed).  Then is "better" show nominal/max CPU freq. instead of actual freq.  (as CPU capabilities only)

NOTE: real-time CPU frequency can be obtained with `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq` and it works fine on Shield but is not refreshed on Kodi GUI.

> Updated to use `CPosixFile` and checked that `GetCPUFrequency()` only is called one time when open hardware info (not auto-refreshed).  Then is "better" show nominal/max CPU freq. instead of actual freq.  (as CPU capabilities only)
> 
> 
> 
> NOTE: real-time CPU frequency can be obtained with `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq` and it works fine on Shield but is not refreshed on Kodi GUI.

I wanted to give you the opportunity to look for yourself but if you read through the code you will find that it is only updated every 15s 🙃

>  it is only updated every 15s

15s is useless. And on Windows is indicated nominal frequency because my CPU is NOT working 3600 Mhz all the time:

![Captura de pantalla 2021-12-15 104356](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/146163620-edb065f9-7322-4270-b3f4-799e44e5509d.png)

And when it is fully loaded it does not work at 3600 either:

![Captura de pantalla 2021-12-15 104817](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/146163777-a06cf824-9ae2-4b1c-86e2-7b692b26f6ea.png)

So what is indicated in Windows is **nominal** CPU frequency.

I still think that the way it is now is correct...

In other words: I do not intend to continue working on this PR. If you think it is better than what we have now it should be approved.

If someone wants to continue improving this: for example indicating the number of cores and the working frequency of each one, the maximum and minimum specification, change update interval to 1s, fix Windows behavior (if is different of the rest of platforms), implement read CPU temperature..... they are free to do it in another PR.

> >  it is only updated every 15s
> 
> 
> 
> 15s is useless. And on Windows is indicated nominal frequency because my CPU is NOT working 3600 Mhz all the time:
> 

That's beside the point really. You said it was static, I pointed out that it's not. If you would like to change it to be quicker you can make a new PR for that 🙂.

I'm sorry that this review is taking so long but that's just how it goes sometimes.

> I have provided a way to resolve the outstanding issues

Your way of resolve ​it is still wrong:

For example: -1 ºC temperature may be valid on a Posix/Linux system if someone uses extreme cooling (liquid nitrogen).

So your solution of marking the -1 ºC temperature as "invalid" is simply not correct and is poorly designed.

Although this is the least considering point 2 and that this PR is Android only

My opinion is that you are blocking a PR for no good reason and this is not right.
Now that `-1` temperature issue has resolved on another PR (https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/20690) we can continue with this 😄

issue_context.title: KODI 19.3 cannot show the CPU info on Firetv 4k Max
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
On Firetv 4k Max, the system info of KODI 19.3 does not show the CPU info. all info is empty.
the info is showing in Kodi 18.9 on Firetv 4k Max.




## Expected Behavior
Show Cpu info



## Actual Behavior
Cpu info is empty.



### Screenshots 
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:
![WechatIMG2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5479289/144353338-6358adba-b353-4af7-a1ac-484c2741b1e6.jpeg)


### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
 - [x] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [ ] tvOS
 - [ ] Linux
 - [ ] OSX
 - [ ] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name: Firetv 4k Max, Android 9
 - Kodi version: 19.3, armv7a 
 - Kodi nightlies version: kodi-20211129-01079c43-Matrix-armeabi-v7a
comments: Mine shows the samething and the memory also shows 100% full why is this happening

Can confirm the hardware info being empty, but memory is fine for me.  
Log: [kodi.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/7650100/kodi.log)

I don't think there's anything useful in there, though.
Memory info issues are fixed by https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/20574

Looks like this is caused by the cpuinfo rework by @lrusak  (https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/16098)
Android was probably using the Linux path in the past. However the regression itself might be intentional, the Android platform should use the android API for that info as much as possible. Kodi doesn't have an android maintainer at the moment so we might well have to deal with it until someone steps up and contributes the feature back (properly) :)

review_comments:
Is there a reason to not use `CCPUInfoPosix`?

That class provides a fallback for reading a script from advancedsettings to allow a user to provide an override for the cpu temperature.

See, https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/ef37e9abaad7c8a188c4656e6b89499b5caecf4a/xbmc/platform/posix/CPUInfoPosix.cpp#L15

Yes, I have two reasons:

1) Eliminate wrong/nonsense temperature indication (-1 ºC).

2) Fallback script can't really be used on Android unless the device is rooted/unlocked.

3) 99.999% of people who use Android on Fire TV Stick or similar they are not interested (I guess) in writing a script to get the CPU temperature (even if could be used on rooted devices). On the contrary, there may be a significant percentage of people who worry and think that something is wrong if they only see empty fields and a temperature of -1 ºC. Because of this, there are even people who care enough to open an Github issue... 😉
